jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher (f/m/d)  in Conservation Genetics and Genetic Monitoring (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: Postdoctoral Researcher (f/m/d) in Conservation Genetics and Genetic MonitoringSenckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN) , headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position in the Department of Genomic Biomonitoring at the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt, starting as of 01.02.2027:**Postdoctoral Researcher (f/m/d) in Conservation Genetics and Genetic Monitoring ****(Full-Time / Part-Time)**Location: FrankfurtEmployment scope: Full-Time / Part-Time options are availableType of contract: Temporary, limited to 2 yearsRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The city of Frankfurt, where the Senckenberg Society was originally founded, hosts the organization’s central administrative services along with two research institutes housing extensive scientific collections and one of Senckenberg’s most renowned institutions, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum Frankfurt. Senckenberg is as much a part of the city’s identity as its skyline and its traditional apple wine.Genetic diversity is a fundamental component of biodiversity, providing the evolutionary potential that allows species and populations to adapt to environmental change. Yet genetic diversity is declining and remains comparatively underrepresented in biodiversity monitoring and policy. At the Genomic Biomonitoring Lab at Senckenberg, we work to address that gap and are seeking a postdoctoral researcher to join us in that aim.The position will focus on how genetic diversity can be measured, monitored and incorporated into practical conservation. This spans from species-level applications to national and international biodiversity policy. The researcher will contribute to ongoing projects on endangered and threatened species where genomics is needed to support management or can be used for monitoring. At the international scale, there is scope to investigate how genetic diversity can be incorporated into global biodiversity frameworks and assessments.We are looking for a researcher who is excited to help shape this emerging research area. The postdoctoral researcher will have the opportunity to develop new research questions and projects under our shared research programme. We are particularly interested in candidates who combine deep scientific curiosity with a motivation to translate ideas into practical conservation impact. Experience working in conservation genetics or genomics is thus essential.Your tasks- Conduct high-quality research on conservation genomics, genetic monitoring and integration of genetic diversity into policy.- Develop and apply approaches for monitoring and protecting genetic diversity in wild populations in Germany and at focal international sites.- Work on connecting genetic diversity with national and international policy.- Collaborate with researchers, conservation organisations, and other stakeholders.- Publish findings in high-quality peer-reviewed journals and present results at international conferences.- Communicate research findings to non-academic audiences, including through policy briefs and communication with conservation managers, and policymakers.- Supervise BSc and/or MSc thesis students.- Help develop international funding proposals for genetic diversity protection and monitoring.Your profile- A PhD in population/conservation/evolutionary genomics or a related field.- At least one year of postdoctoral research experience.- Hands-on experience with genomic datasets.- Experience in conservation biology and biodiversity protection, including collaboration with conservation practitioners, managers, or policy makers.- A strong publication record appropriate to your career stage.Desirable skills- Excellent scientific writing and communication skills in English.- Experience or a strong interest in developing research proposals and securing third-party funding.- A collaborative, collegial and well-organised approach to research and teamwork.We offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.Senckenberg is certified under the audit berufundfamilie programme and is committed to promoting a better work-life balance.How to apply?Please upload your applicationelectronically as a single PDF by 05.12.2026, containing:- A letter of motivation (1-2 pages), including clear explanations about your interest in the position and an outline of how your experience fits the research programme.- CV and publication list.- PhD certificate.- Contact details for two academic refereesPlease upload your application by clicking on the "Apply Online" button in the bottom of this announcement. Applications via email cannot be considered.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt am MainFor specific questions about this role, please contact Prof. Dr. Deborah Leighat deborah.leigh@senckenberg.de

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Plant Interaction Ecology (m/f/d) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/d) in Plant Interaction EcologySenckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN) , headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre (SBiK-F), starting as of 01.02.2027 :Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/d) in Plant Interaction Ecology(Full-Time / Part-Time ** ** options available)Location: Frankfurt am MainEmployment scope: Full-Time; Part-Time options are availableType of contract: Temporary, limited to 3 yearsRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The mission of the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre is to study the complex interactions between biodiversity, climate and society.The announced position is part of a newly established research group studying plant environment interactions. The successful candidate will contribute to shaping the group's research programme and develop an independent research project aligned with the group's broader interests.Your tasks- Conduct internationally recognized research on how plant-animal interactions shape plant regeneration- Advance a mechanistic understanding of how plant-animal interactions and regeneration processes influence plant responses to climate and land-use change, e.g., shifts in species ranges or ecological novelty- Design and conduct field experiments, e.g., testing drivers of plant establishment, intraspecific variability, or the role of animal-mediated seed dispersal in forest dynamics- Develop and apply ecological models that integrate experimental findings with long-term datasets, linking individual-level processes to population dynamics and species range shifts- Publish research findings in leading international, peer-reviewed journals- Develop competitive proposals for third-party research funding- Supervise and mentor BSc, MSc, and PhD students- Contribute to teaching at the Bachelor’s and Master’s levels- Contribute to the development of the Interaction Ecology and Climate research groupYour profile- A doctoral degree, completed or nearing completion, in ecology, botany, biology, or a closely related field- A strong background in ecology, with research experience in plant ecology and or interactions between plants and animals- Demonstrated experience in designing and conducting field experiments- Experience conducting fieldwork under challenging conditions, e.g., in alpine environments or remote forest areas- Strong quantitative skills, including experience with advanced statistical methods such as Bayesian hierarchical models and data integration (combining heterogeneous datasets) and/or demographic or process-based population models, preferably using R- A strong publication record relative to career stage- Motivation to develop independent research on plant regeneration and biotic interactions in the context of climate and land-use change- Ability to work independently and collaboratively, and a willingness to contribute to teaching and student supervision- Fluency in spoken and written EnglishDesirable skills- An interest in science communication and public outreach- Proficiency in German, particularly for contributing to teaching and outreach activitiesWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV with a full publication list, copies of certificates and diplomas, along with the names of two referees) as a single PDF by 13 December 2026.Apply online via:https://short.sg/j/68770090by pressing the "Apply now" ButtonApplications via email cannot be considered.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt am MainFor specific questions about this role, please contact Prof. Dr. Eike Lena Neuschulz at:eike-lena.neuschulz@senckenberg.de****For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/Please visit our website at www.senckenberg.de for further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung.
